title: Pay out only what the ATM's notes can make

blocks.text: An ATM network is adding machines in Seoul and Kuwait City to its euro machines. Each machine pays out only whole notes of its currency, up to a maximum per withdrawal, and the server refuses anything else before the cash dispenser is asked. The table of notes and maximums, `CASSETTES`, is in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/CashWithdrawal.java`, and so is the participant, which already answers every request it can read.

items: `decide(...)`: the answer for an amount the server could read.

blocks.text: When you're done, every withdrawal gets a response in the Context, whatever the ATM put in its fields, and the won and dinar machines pay out what their cardholders asked for. About fifteen lines in total.
The tests hand `prepare` each request the way the server's channel would: packed by the ATM's side and unpacked with `iso87ascii.xml`.

cases.says: a withdrawal the euro notes can make, within the maximum, is approved
an amount that is not a whole number of the smallest note is refused with 13
an amount above the currency's maximum is refused with 61
a currency the ATM holds no notes for is refused with 57
a request without field 49 gets a 30 response instead of an exception, since a missing field reads as null
a field 4 with a sign is not twelve digits and gets 30, though BigDecimal would accept it
field 4 in won counts whole won, since the won has no minor unit
field 4 in Kuwaiti dinars has three decimals, taken from the currency rather than assumed
a currency code ISOCurrency doesn't know gets 30 instead of an exception

origin.section: 6.3 An Amount Counts the Minor Units of the Currency in Field 49

concepts: Field 4 counts the minor units of the currency in field 49, whose decimals come from the currency, and an unknown currency must be answered rather than thrown.
The packager checks a numeric field's length, not its characters, so field 4 must be checked for twelve digits before it is converted.
